'''Aaron James Henry''' (born August 30, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Nagoya Diamond Dolphins]] of the Japanese [[B.League]]. He previously played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]].

==Early life==
Henry was born in [[Louisville, Kentucky]] but moved to [[Indianapolis|Indianapolis, Indiana]] while he was a child.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/880096/2019/03/21/the-voice-in-aaron-henrys-head/|title=The voice in Aaron Henry's head|first=Brendan|last=Quinn|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=March 21, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref> He attended [[Ben Davis High School]], where he was a four-year starter on the school's basketball team. As a junior, he averaged 14.2 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists per game and was named to the first team of the Indy-Area Super Team by the ''[[Indianapolis Star]]'' and second team All-State by the [[Associated Press]] as he helped lead the Giants to the 2017 4A State Championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/three-star-state-forward-aaron-164326122.html|title=Three-Star In-State Forward Aaron Henry Has Big Ten, Big East Interest|first=Stu|last=Jackson|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=April 9, 2017|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref> Henry led the Giants to a sectional title while averaging 17 points, 8.8 rebounds and four assists in his senior season and was named first team All-State by the Associated Press and to the second team by ''[[USA Today]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/missouri/Article/Michigan-State-Spartans-basketball-recruiting-Aaron-Henry-makes-big-jump-in-final-Top247-for-2018-117489553/|title=MSU signee Aaron Henry makes big jump in final Top247 for 2018|first=Jeremy|last=Warnemuende|date=April 19, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref> A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] over offers from [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/09/11/ben-davis-forward-aaron-henry-commits-michigan-state/653923001/|title=Ben Davis' Aaron Henry commits to Michigan State|first=Kyle|last=Neddenriep|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=September 11, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman Henry played in all 39 of Michigan State's games, starting 22 of the final 23 contests and averaging 6.1 points and 3.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/2019/07/10/michigan-state-basketball-aaron-henry/1690065001/|title=Michigan State basketball's Aaron Henry preparing for dynamite sophomore season|first=Gregory|last=Levinsky|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=July 10, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref> He averaged 9 points and 5.6 rebounds during postseason play as whole and 10.4 points and 5.2 rebounds in the NCAA Tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2019/10/michigan-states-aaron-henry-looks-to-pick-up-where-he-left-off-from-strong-final-four-run.html|title=Michigan State's Aaron Henry looks to pick up where he left off from strong Final Four run|first=Mike|last=Mulholland|website=[[MLive.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state-university/2019/04/29/michigan-state-spartans-aaron-henry-pegged-rising-basketball-star/3618452002/|title=Michigan State Spartans' Aaron Henry pegged as rising basketball star|work=[[The Detroit News]]|date=April 29, 2019}}</ref> Henry scored a season high 20 points to go with eight rebounds and six assists against [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] in the Sweet Sixteen of the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2828614-aaron-henry-no-2-michigan-state-crush-tremont-waters-no-3-lsu-in-sweet-16|title=Aaron Henry, No. 2 Michigan State Crush Tremont Waters, No. 3 LSU in Sweet 16|first=Tyler|last=Conway|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=March 29, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref>

As a junior, Henry averaged 15.4 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game. He was named third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]]. Following the season he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gastelum |first1=Andrew |title=Michigan State Forward Aaron Henry Declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/04/12/michigan-state-forward-aaron-henry-declares-for-nba-draft |access-date=June 30, 2021 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=April 12, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia 76ers (2021–2022)===
After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Henry signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on August 8, 2021, splitting time with their G League affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].<ref>{{cite web|title=76ers Sign Aaron Henry, Re-Sign Rayjon Tucker to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-aaron-henry-re-sign-rayjon-tucker-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=August 8, 2021|access-date=August 14, 2021}}</ref> Henry was waived by the 76ers on January 11, 2022.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Levick |first1=Noah |title=Local product Brown Jr. earns two-way contract with Sixers |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/sixers-charlie-brown-jr-contract-aaron-henry-tyrese-maxey-sixers-roster |access-date=January 11, 2022 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=January 11, 2022}}</ref>

===Delaware Blue Coats (2022)===
On January 18, 2022, Henry was reacquired and activated by the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 18, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2022}}</ref>

===Metropolitans 92 (2022–2023)===
On August 6, 2022, he has signed with [[Metropolitans 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/aaron-henry-inks-with-metropolitans-92/|title=Aaron Henry inks with Metropolitans 92|last=|first=|date=August 6, 2022|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 15, 2022}}</ref> He suffered a season-ending quadriceps injury in December 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Boulogne-levallois-va-devoir-se-passer-d-aaron-henry-pendant-plusieurs-semaines/1369411|title=Boulogne-Levallois va devoir se passer d'Aaron Henry pendant plusieurs semaines|work=[[L'Équipe]]|date=December 10, 2022|access-date=June 26, 2023|language=French}}</ref>

=== Fighting Eagles Nagoya (2023–2025) ===
On June 30, 2023, Henry signed with [[Fighting Eagles Nagoya]] of the [[Japan]]ese [[B.League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-30 |title=【#11 アーロン・ヘンリー選手】新規入団のお知らせ |url=https://www.fightingeagles.jp/news/detail/id=15657 |access-date=2023-07-02 |website=ファイティングイーグルス名古屋 |language=ja}}</ref> On May 28, 2024, he re-signed with Fighting Eagles Nagoya.<ref>{{cite web |title=【2024-25シーズン】#11 アーロン・ヘンリー 選手 契約継続のお知らせ |url=https://www.fightingeagles.jp/news/detail/id=16409 |publisher=ファイティングイーグルス名古屋 |access-date=24 November 2024 |date=28 May 2024}}</ref>

=== Nagoya Diamond Dolphins (2025–present) ===
On June 11, 2025, Henry signed with [[Nagoya Diamond Dolphins]] of the [[Japan]]ese [[B.League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-11 |title=【アーロン・ヘンリー 選手 B.LEAGUE 2025-26 SEASON契約合意（新規）のお知らせ |url=https://nagoya-dolphins.jp/news/detail/id=19829 |access-date=2025-10-26 |website=名古屋ダイヤモンドドルフィンズ |language=ja}}</ref>
